title: Indirect Object Pronouns (me, te, le, nos, les)

sections.content: Indirect object pronouns answer the question 'to whom?' or 'for whom?' an action is performed. They are placed immediately before conjugated verbs.

sections.title: Indirect Object Pronouns
rows: Él me da un regalo. (He gives me a gift.)
Yo te digo la verdad. (I tell you the truth.)
Le mando un mensaje a Juan. (I send Juan a message.)
El profesor nos explica la lección. (The teacher explains to us.)
Les presto dinero a mis amigos. (I lend money to my friends.)

items.spanish: Mi madre me cocina todos los domingos.
items.english: My mother cooks for me every Sunday.
I asked the receptionist for help.
Will you lend us your umbrella?

sections.content: Spanish often uses BOTH the indirect pronoun AND the noun phrase in the same sentence: 'Le di el libro a Carlos' (literally: 'To him I gave the book to Carlos'). This is standard and expected.
